subject.declared_domain: The C0->C3 semantic-compression FIDELITY GATE for the Semantic Control Plane. Its own declared job (module docstring): prove that C0->C3 is lossy-abstraction compression WITH a lossless decompression path back to lexical evidence -- a deterministic lexical ruleset, never a latent representation. Supplies the Node type, decompress() and fidelity_check() that the C2/C3 materializers build on.

methodology.how: Two operations over a hand-built Node tree, both declared deterministic with zero ML: ladder(node) shows the compression upward (fact -> interaction -> motif -> system) and the decompression downward to exact lexical evidence; fidelity_check(node) is THE GATE -- it asserts every C1+ node decompresses to a C0 that carries real lexical evidence, failing any C1+ with no children as LATENT (embedding-like, 'the build drifted toward ML') and any C0 with no provenance.evidence as ungrounded. The extension points are a recognizer SDK (C0 emitters) and a rule SDK (C0->C1->C2->C3). THE BURIED OPINIONS, ENUMERATED IN PROSE because the TO's form is prose (see evidence): (1) the ENTIRE C0 layer is produced by TEXT REGEXES OVER SOURCE FILES, not by importing values -- recognize_iam_cross_firm_deny() parses cot-pipeline/iam.tf and recognize_pipeline_map() parses .tools/safe_deploy_core.py with the literal pattern '"([a-z_]+)":\s*\("([a-z0-9\-]+)",\s*"([a-z]+)"\)' at :107; (2) the reference demonstration is HARDCODED TO ONE FIRM -- build_firm_sep_ladder() passes the literal 'cot' at :247; (3) exactly 2 recognizers and 4 rules exist, so the covered artifact classes are the two that were built first; (4) a C1+ node with no children is DEFINED as latent, which makes 'has children' the operative test for 'is not an embedding'.
declared_opinions: The ENTIRE C0 layer is produced by TEXT REGEXES OVER SOURCE FILES rather than by importing values: recognize_iam_cross_firm_deny() parses cot-pipeline/iam.tf and recognize_pipeline_map() parses .tools/safe_deploy_core.py with a literal string-tuple pattern at :107. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: the input was legitimately refactored to a dict comprehension and the parser silently stopped matching.

The reference demonstration is HARDCODED TO ONE FIRM -- build_firm_sep_ladder() passes the literal 'cot' at :247, so the proof the substrate is lexical-deterministic is demonstrated on one firm's separation only.
Exactly 2 recognizers and 4 rules exist, so the artifact classes the gate can be run against are the two that were built first, not a governed set.
A C1+ node with no children is DEFINED as latent (embedding-like), which makes 'has children' the operative test for 'is not an ML approximation' -- a structural proxy for a semantic property.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: TWO different behaviours at two layers, and they disagree. (a) THE RECOGNIZER FAILS SILENTLY: recognize_pipeline_map() returns a CLEAN EMPTY LIST when its regex matches nothing -- no exception, no warning, no log. (b) THE ENTRYPOINT FAILS LOUDLY: `python comp_ladder.py` exits rc=1 with an uncaught StopIteration traceback, because rule_c1_allowed_edge :134 calls a bare next() with no default over the empty list from (a).
silent_degrade_paths: ⛔ THE LOUDNESS IS ACCIDENTAL, NOT DESIGNED, AND THAT IS THIS CARD'S MOST IMPORTANT ROW. The only reason a zero-recognizer result is visible at all is a bare next() two functions downstream. Any caller that instead wrote next(..., None), used a for-loop, or guarded with `if c0_pmap:` would convert this same condition into a SILENT EMPTY LADDER -- and an empty ladder passes fidelity_check trivially, because a tree with no C1+ nodes has no node that fails the LATENT test.

A partially-empty C0 layer degrades the same way: recognize_iam_cross_firm_deny and recognize_pipeline_map fail independently, so one recognizer going quiet leaves a ladder that still builds and still passes the gate over the half that survived.
Because nothing is persisted (see artifact.persistence), a passing fidelity_check and a never-run fidelity_check leave byte-identical traces: none.

verdict.why: A measured defect blocks load-bearing use: THE FIDELITY GATE CANNOT CURRENTLY RUN ITS OWN REFERENCE DEMONSTRATION. `python comp_ladder.py` exits rc=1 on an uncaught StopIteration, because 1 of its 2 C0 recognizers returns zero against the live estate -- exercised, with a control that fired, and isolated to the input's shape rather than the parser's correctness. THE SUBSTANTIVE HARM, and it is larger than a crashing demo: this module's declared purpose is to PROVE the substrate is lexical-deterministic rather than a latent ML representation, and that proof is exactly what currently does not execute. The C2/C3 materializers still import Node and fidelity_check successfully, so the estate is not broken -- but the artifact whose job is to demonstrate the property is not demonstrating it. ⛔ NOT SOFTENED: the module is careful, well-documented work whose gate logic reads correctly and whose failure is loud rather than silent, and 6 downstream materializers depend on it without incident. A well-built gate that cannot run its own proof is still UNSOUND as substrate, and the two are different objects. THE MOST TRANSFERABLE FINDING IS NOT THE CRASH BUT ITS OPPOSITE: the crash is a GIFT. It is produced by a bare next() with no default, two functions below a recognizer that fails silently -- so the visibility is an accident of one unguarded call, and the ordinary defensive fix (a default, a guard, a for-loop) would convert a loud failure into a silent empty ladder that passes the gate vacuously. || SEMANTIC-AXIS DECLARATION: NOT SYSTEMATICALLY EXAMINED, stated explicitly so silence does not read as clean. The four opinions enumerated in methodology.how were forced into view by the failure_mode and coverage rows, not found by a deliberate sweep. I did NOT audit whether the LATENT test (a C1+ with no children) is still the ruled definition, whether the 2 built recognizers are the 2 that matter, or whether hardcoding 'cot' as the reference firm still reflects intent. ⛔ And no instrument I used can reach that axis: rc, tracebacks, grep counts and source reads are all blind to a deprecated opinion. || GENERATOR CURRENCY: materializer_standing='not_applicable' -- this module materializes no layer, so the currency question does not arise for it. That is a MEASURED absence of applicability, not an unmeasured currency (2.0.0_SA_COO~X 73308's distinction: NOT_APPLICABLE where absence is measured, UNVERIFIED where a generator exists and currency was not established).
